    Team tactics

    Field, scoring and restarts

    Throw from green quadrants. Run or hand off in the yellow runway. Every role can use the entire blue center zone. Only Anchors can enter the opposite half. Airborne passes may cross above the dirt strips. A carried ball, intentional bounce, deflection or loose ball touching dirt is out of bounds, and the opponent takes a quadrant reset. More than three uninterrupted seconds unblocked in the ring gives the opponent a free run lane.

    The lob is the standard, high-arching pass. Bounce passes are slower and easier to handle but stay on one half. Line drives are fastest and flattest but harder to catch. Nearby unpressured teammates can use a safe low underhand lob or a direct handoff. Low Arm Strength and Accuracy create more short-hops; low Accuracy can also sail a throw over the receiver.

    Carry through the ring for 2, or catch a teammate’s pass in blue and finish for 3. A center interception or fumble recovery earns 1 and possession. Catch a legal airborne save kick in blue for 5. A tie goes to runway-only sudden death. The next score wins.

    A quadrant tackle gives the carrier a stationary throw. A runway tackle turns it over. A center catch stopped short retains possession. Incompletions stay live unless the ball lands or rolls out of bounds. Strength, size and support drive two-to-25-second piles; Tackling and IQ can end them, while carriers may pull out, fumble, sneak a handoff or risk a wild pass. Defenders can also strip the ball using Strength, Hands, Reaction and IQ. Ordinary stoppages hold for two seconds; free-run penalties hold for three before formation.

    Match field

    Field guide

    Both teams attack the 4-yard ring inside the 10-yard center zone. A tackle short of the ring stops the finish. Watch for Anchors blocking off the ball, slipping toward the ring or drawing a defender away from a cut. Carry in for two or catch in the blue and finish for three. Watch the gold ball and its shadow to read the height of a pass or bounce. Gold outlines show blocks and pile drives. On fumbles, only players with a realistic arrival path pursue; nearby markers dive, fall and shove around a grounded ball while distant players preserve team shape. A center catch directly from an airborne kick save earns five. New match draws two fresh squads.
